summary: Sends CHOP channels to DMX, Art-Net, sACN, KiNET, FTDI, or ENTTEC-style outputs, with routing-table, serial, network, rate, and universe controls.
key_concepts: Sends CHOP channels to DMX, Art-Net, sACN, KiNET, or FTDI targets using DMX values in the 0-255 range.
Input channel order maps directly to consecutive DMX addresses unless Packet Per Channel mode is used to pack samples into universe channels.
DMX512 output should respect the documented 44 Hz maximum refresh limit, so Rate above 44 is not reliable for physical DMX devices.
Art-Net Net, Subnet, and Universe are protocol addresses; Network Address selects the receiving IP or broadcast target.
A Routing Table can route packet-per-channel output by net, subnet, universe, and netaddress, falling back to the operator parameters when columns are missing.
ArtSync can synchronize multi-universe ArtDmx output by waiting for packets to send before emitting a sync packet.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Connect to output device or network

key_params.name: interface
key_params.note: Enttec serial/USB, Art-Net, sACN, KiNET, or related output mode

key_params.name: packetpersample
key_params.note: Each channel maps to a DMX address

key_params.name: packetperchan
key_params.note: Each sample in a channel maps to a DMX address

common_gotchas: DMX values are 0-255 and channel order maps directly to consecutive DMX addresses unless packet-per-channel is used.
DMX512 devices have a maximum refresh rate of about 44 Hz; official docs recommend Rate <= 44 for reliability.
Packet Per Sample and Packet Per Channel imply different channel/sample layouts, so generated plans must choose deliberately.
On macOS, ENTTEC USB Pro may require unloading the AppleUSBFTDI kernel extension before connection.
Broadcast addresses are convenient but can flood networks; prefer explicit receiver IPs for show-critical systems.
